original_poem:
تٕو آدرِس پٲٹھ چھٕ کتھ پٲنچھ کھسےٚ وْٹھی؟  
خانہ خرَبات سنی سیٚتھ چھیُ وچھیُ؟  
زوٚنِم بَرٔ تہِ یوٚدُر بٲپتھ پٲٹھ وچھ وٚوٚدم  
کٹھیُم غِبار سڑُ، پٲٹھ خرےٚ دریشہٚس کۄچھٲی؟
translated_poem:
I went looking for you—where did you vanish?  
The tavern was deserted—have you left it too?  
I went from street to street in search of you,  
All I found was dust—where is the door to your house?

stanzas.loss_note: خانہ خرَبات (khāna-e-kharābāt) is a Sufi technical term meaning the tavern of ruin — a sacred space of spiritual dissolution and divine intoxication in the Rishi-Sufi tradition; the translation renders it merely as 'deserted tavern', losing the mystical register entirely.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: the Sufi tavern of spiritual ruin where the seeker dissolves into the divine
the dust of futile searching left behind by the absent beloved
the threshold of the divine that remains forever out of reach

cultural_entities.translation_note: In Kashmiri Sufi poetry rooted in the Rishi order and Sheikh Nooruddin's tradition, the kharābāt is not a literal tavern but the sacred space of ego-annihilation and mystical intoxication; 'deserted tavern' strips this of its spiritual meaning.
